code_review.finding: Verifier LoRA is rank 16 on q/k/v/o in the last 12 language layers, 5,111,808 parameters. It does not train the vision encoder or alter the 4096-to-3072 condition projection.
Reference/generated RGB and the observation-first teacher use no_grad; student uses detached RGB. Only verifier LoRA requires gradients in calibration; Wan, C and the Qwen base are frozen.
Generation explicitly disables verifier LoRA. Verifier reads bind the role in the checkpoint closure; block recomputation captures the same role.
Vision and language block checkpointing remains enabled in eval mode. RGB/adapter gradients agree with plain evaluation in native tiny-Qwen tests.

New H and Q test: four reference/generated microbatches per update, two updates, checkpointed vs plain gradients and AdamW parameters agree. Only verifier parameters change; generator/base/vision/C remain bitwise unchanged.

Frozen and LoRA share selected native decoder and visual patch construction; 81 video frames, stride 3 plus final RGB frame => 28 observations at 480x832; 4096-wide messages project to 3072 only at final Wan interface.

First Q attempt ended after saved interface step 32; verifier LoRA calibration had not begun. Last retries start from step 64. H previously performed one real calibration update with nonzero verifier-only gradient before a subsequent SIGKILL.

Repeated retries had used the same failing GPU and the four-step save interval lost H step 65. New jobs reject that GPU UUID, checkpoint each update and trace microbatch execution. Scheduler itself is not modified.

limitations: CPU tests use small native Qwen with tiny/fake Wan fixtures; full-size GPU execution is checked separately.
SIGKILL sender is still unknown; device association is not proof of a hardware defect or proof that no platform-specific software issue exists.
Frozen and LoRA old jobs used different GPU types, so old success/failure does not isolate the adapter effect.
A completed training run is not evidence of improved video physics quality.
